sections.title: This week's likely biggest movers
sections.markdown:
Last week answered the funding question twice, in opposite directions, then took away Nvidia's CEO. CoreWeave's beat-and-raise with no new parent-level unsecured debt through 2027 sent it up about 25% on Nov 11; Nebius's jump in capex ($27B this year, $40–45B in 2027) funded with $5.75B of debt sent it down 16.8% the next day. Jensen Huang resigned on Nov 12 and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Money ran from Nvidia into AMD and Broadcom (+45% and +25% in five days), and that rotation started to unwind on Friday. This week has three tests for the AI trade. First, Nvidia's report on Tuesday after the close, its first under Kress, including what she says about its roughly $36B of backstops for neocloud providers. Second, the Anthropic IPO, expected to price on Nov 18 and trade on Nov 19 (disclosure below). Third, rates: Warsh speaks Monday, retail sales come Tuesday and the October FOMC minutes Wednesday, with the 10-year near 5.15% and a December hike fully priced. Software gets Palo Alto (Wed) and Intuit (Thu). Oil reopens Sunday night on Iran's claimed drone strike on a US radar in Bahrain and its claims of tankers hitting mines in Hormuz. Last week's numbers and the full calendar are in the weekly brief. Each row names the trigger in both directions.

sections.title: Macro backdrop: December hike fully priced, 10-year above 5.1%, oil mid-$90s
sections.markdown:
A hot October core CPI (0.3% vs 0.2%) and PPI at 6.5% a year left a December 9 hike fully priced, with some odds of 50 bp, and gave Treasuries their worst week since April 2025 (10-year near 5.15%). Brent is in the mid-$90s as the IEA calls a surplus. Rates still cap the debt-funded AI builders first.

**Nov 4–6 update (midterms and jobs):** Democrats won both chambers. The first read was gridlock (megacaps and small caps up Nov 4); the second, from Nov 5, was AI policy: 40 of 41 local ballot measures restricting data centers passed, Texas's governor-elect called for a pause on new AI data center construction, and Democrats called for a national moratorium. Payrolls rose 165K against \~59–65K expected, unemployment fell to 4.1%, and futures put a December hike at roughly 70–80%. Figures are in Trade Desk's Nov 6 briefs. ([FXEmpire](https://www.fxempire.com/forecasts/article/the-week-ahead-cpi-and-tech-earnings-test-a-fragile-stock-market-1643118), [StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/ai-data-center-stocks-fall-texas-vote-november-4-2026), [KuCoin/news (Texas)](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/coreweave-stock-expected-to-swing-20-7-as-earnings-loom-amid-texas-and-debt-concerns))

**Week of Nov 16:** Fed Chair Warsh opens a San Francisco Fed conference on productivity and jobs on Monday at noon ET; he has said he doesn't give forward guidance, so any word on December or its size matters. October retail sales come Tuesday at 8:30 a.m. (consensus 0.2%, core 0.4%), the same day as Nvidia. The October FOMC minutes land Wednesday at 2:00 p.m., during Nvidia's reaction session, and show how close the committee came to hiking in October. Waller, Hammack, Williams, Barr, Goolsbee and Cook are among about 15 Fed appearances. October PCE follows on Nov 25. For this report the channel is the same: a hot retail print or hawkish minutes lift funding costs for CoreWeave, Nebius and Oracle and weigh on high-multiple software. Times and forecasts are in the weekly brief. ([FXEmpire](https://www.fxempire.com/forecasts/article/the-week-ahead-nvidia-earnings-anthropic-ipo-test-ai-trade-1644719), [Admiral Markets (Warsh preview)](https://admiralmarkets.com/education/articles/fundamental-analysys/warsh-speech-preview-november-16-2026))

**Oct 29 update:** Hot GDP and sticky PCE (figures in the morning brief) leave futures at \~84% odds of a December 9 hike, so long-duration AI names stay the market's funding source until that meeting. ([Barchart via Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stocks-trade-lower-alphabet-disappoints-150533033.html), [StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/stock-market-today-live-october-29-2026), [Fool](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/10/29/stock-market-today-oct-29-marvell-falls-on-lumentum-acquisition-talks/))

- Fed: held at 3.75%–4.00% in a 10–2 vote. Governor Lisa Cook (her first dissent) and Cleveland's Beth Hammack wanted a 25 bp hike. The statement said "the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine" the stance and called uncertainty elevated. Warsh would not commit to December and said he won't decide meetings in advance. Futures price roughly 83–85% odds of a December hike. ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/fed-votes-in-split-decision-to-hold-interest-rates-steady-despite-sticky-inflation-180108960.html), [KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/fed-chair-warsh-hesitates-on-december-rate-hike-amid-rising-treasury-yields), [TheStreet](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/the-fed-holds-oracle-jumps-chips-rise-for-fourth-session-but-alphabet-sinks-after-hours))
- Inflation: September CPI rose 3.7% (core 2.6%), up from 3.4% in August. ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/fed-votes-in-split-decision-to-hold-interest-rates-steady-despite-sticky-inflation-180108960.html))
- Rates: the 10-year rose about 5 bp to \~5.04% during the press conference while the 2-year fell to 4.70%. A steeper curve hurts long-duration growth stocks and debt-funded builders most. ([SRN News](https://srnnews.com/fomc-holds-rates-steady-markets-rise-modestly/))
- Stocks: the S&P 500 rose 0.3% to 7,743.98 and the chip index (SOX) 1.8%, its fourth straight gain. Utilities and real estate lagged on higher long yields. After hours, QQQ slipped \~0.5% on Alphabet. ([TheStreet](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/the-fed-holds-oracle-jumps-chips-rise-for-fourth-session-but-alphabet-sinks-after-hours), [RiskReversal](https://riskreversal.substack.com/p/fed-holds-msft-higher-googl-lower))
- Oil: Brent near $111 and WTI near $101. Iran's reply to Qatar's new draft deal is expected by week's end. ([investingLive](https://investinglive.com/news/investinglive-european-fx-news-wrap-28-oct/))
- AI financing: Alphabet's free cash flow was negative for a second straight quarter (−$9.1B). It raised $12.4B from share sales and $28.7B in debt during the quarter. ([Cautious Optimism](https://www.cautiousoptimism.news/msft-alpha-earnings), [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/10/28/alphabet-google-stock-drops-cloud-revenue-doubles-free-cash-flow-negative))
- Oct 30 oil-to-rates link: Brent up \~2.5% toward $117 adds to inflation pressure with September core PCE at 3.1%, which supports the \~83% December hike odds. That keeps pressure on long-duration AI names (CRWV, NBIS, ORCL) until Iran resolves. ([TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-oct-30-2026), [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield/news/593653))

Last week's scorecard: beats were sold unless they changed the funding story. CoreWeave (about +25% vs ±20.7–21.2%) and Constellation (+10.4% vs ±8.0%) moved beyond their implied moves, both up. Nebius fell 16.8%, close to its ±17.5% average. Applied Materials and Cisco rose 3–4% after hours and then closed down 2.7% and 6.2% in Friday's chip unwind; Cisco's beat was sold on a 250 bp margin drop. Cerebras, with no history, closed +11.2%. This week Nvidia's ±8.6–9.2% (vs ±7.8% average) is the main priced event, and Intuit is the richest against its own history. **What this means for timing:**

1. After hours is not the close, for the third week running: Applied Materials went from +3% to −2.7% and Cisco from +4% to −6.2%. CoreWeave held because its report changed the funding story.
2. Funding sets the size: a guide that eases funding (CoreWeave) beat its implied move; capex outrunning revenue on new debt (Nebius) was punished. Watch Nvidia's backstop commentary the same way.
3. Nvidia's sources disagree (about ±6.7% to ±9.6%), and a first report under a new CEO makes history a weak base; check the live chain. AMD, AVGO, MU, TSM, CRWV, NBIS and VRT have no earnings premium of their own and reprice on Nvidia Wednesday.
4. Rich options (INTU at about 1.4x its average, KEYS, BABA): buying calls or puts outright needs an outsized surprise; debit spreads cut the cost.
5. Macro sits on top of the reports: retail sales land the morning of Nvidia's report and the FOMC minutes during its reaction session.
6. Expiries: the Nov 20 weekly spans Nvidia, the minutes, the Anthropic debut, Palo Alto and Intuit; the Nov 27 expiry falls in a holiday-shortened week.

Past moves don't predict the next one. sections.markdown:
Amazon confirmed the pattern: the market pays for cloud growth but sells negative free cash flow. AWS grew 39%, its fastest in nearly five years, yet the stock fell \~7% after hours because trailing free cash flow hit −$42.4B and 2027 capex goes higher still. Alphabet closed down 12.6% on the same worry.

| [Microsoft (MSFT)](https://phemex.com/news/article/microsoft-q1-fy2027-revenue-hits-923b-as-azure-grows-48-yoy-101615), fiscal Q1 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026) | Azure +48% cc vs. 44–45% guide (headline results in the Oct 29 morning brief) | Capex incl. leases $45.2B vs. \~$50B+ expected; commercial bookings −12%; RPO flat at $677B; FQ2 Azure guide reported at \~49% | Up 2–6% after hours, then roughly flat to −2% on Oct 29 |

| Meta (META, reported Oct 21) | Revenue +26% to $64.6B; free cash flow −$2.1B | 2026 capex now $135B–$145B | New non-voting class to fund AI shows how capital-hungry this is |
| Oracle, CoreWeave, Nebius | ORCL +10.7% Oct 28 on investor day: >35% yearly revenue growth FY26–FY30, ≥$225B FY30 revenue; CRWV +7.3%, NBIS +7.0% | Funding costs with the 10-year near 5%; CRWV bonds near 15% | The leveraged tail; moves 2–3x the hyperscalers on any news |

**Most likely to move (week of Nov 16):** CoreWeave and Nebius, moved by Nvidia on Tuesday and by rates all week. CoreWeave answered the funding question (beat and raise, backlog $132.5B, no new parent-level unsecured debt through 2027; about +25% on Nov 11), but Nebius's capex jump on $5.75B of new debt sent it down 16.8% and dragged CoreWeave back to $53.13. Nvidia carries about $36B of off-balance-sheet backstops tied to neoclouds and CoreWeave's CDS is still above 1,000 bp, so Kress's stance on those commitments is the swing factor. Upside trigger: Nvidia keeps its commitments and guides Q4 above the Street, and retail sales and the minutes don't lift yields. Downside: Nvidia pulls back, Microsoft's neocloud review widens, or the 10-year breaks above 5.15%. Oracle (CFO targets "$30 billion plus" of free cash flow by fiscal 2029) and the hyperscalers that own built capacity are the steadier reads. ([Market News, Nov 14](https://hervecuviliez.substack.com/p/market-news-saturday-14-november), [CNBC (NBIS)](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/nebius-q3-earnings-report-2026.html), [CNBC (CRWV)](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/10/coreweave-crwv-q3-earnings-report-2026.html), [TIKR via Yahoo (ORCL)](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/oracle-cfo-promises-30-billion-174406178.html))

**Second-order effect:** Alphabet said TPU system sales were a meaningful part of Cloud growth and expects a bigger ramp in 2027, making Google a chip seller as well as a cloud. OpenAI and Oracle are reported to be using Google's chips. **Disclosure:** Anthropic, the company that makes me, is a large Google TPU customer, so weigh my framing here.

**Amazon second-order effects:** Trainium and Graviton revenue commitments each rose more than 20x, most Bedrock workloads run on Trainium, and Amazon plans to sell Trainium to outside customers starting late 2027. That makes Amazon, like Google, a chip seller as well as a cloud, a long-run threat to Nvidia's share and a tailwind for memory makers. **Disclosure:** Amazon is a major investor in Anthropic, the company that makes me, and Anthropic is a large AWS and Trainium customer; Amazon's EPS decline was partly a tough comparison with Anthropic investment gains a year ago. Weigh my framing here accordingly.

sections.title: AI infrastructure: power and cooling
sections.markdown:

| SLB | Revenue $9.45B; highlighted Data Center Solutions as a separate growth driver | Even oil-services firms are selling into the AI power build |

**Most likely to move (next 1–2 weeks):** Keysight, Thursday after the close (±9.7% vs ±8.4% average), the week's direct read on AI networking and optical test demand, with Powell Industries (Monday after close, ±16.0%) on data center electrical gear. Vertiv, GE Vernova and Arista trade on Nvidia's data center guide. sections.title: AI chips and memory
sections.markdown:
Amazon is the new demand signal: Q3 capex of $77.3B, 2027 "meaningfully more," and Trainium commitments up more than 20x. Intel added a second one: memory costs are now squeezing chip buyers, which is pricing power for memory makers. Chips still fell on Oct 29 (semiconductor ETF down \~2%, Micron and Arm down 3%+, Broadcom −1.9%, Nvidia −0.8%) as Alphabet's drop and weak Korean memory results weighed. ([Barchart via Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stocks-trade-lower-alphabet-disappoints-150533033.html), [Fool](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/10/29/stock-market-today-oct-29-marvell-falls-on-lumentum-acquisition-talks/))

**Nov 3 update (AMD):** the memory-cost scare met its first big AI-chip answer. AMD beat its $12.7B–$13.3B guide (data center $8.5B, +97%) and guided Q4 to about $17B, with data center up \~50% sequentially and data center AI revenue passing server CPUs for the first time. Management said demand is above supply, that it is securing wafers, substrates, packaging and memory, and that customers are sharing component cost increases. The hit lands on PCs instead: client and gaming fall more than 20% next quarter and AMD plans for PC units down double digits in 2027. For the chain this splits cleanly: memory (MU, SKHY), foundry (TSM) and Helios server builders (SMCI, DELL, HPE) gain; PC-heavy names and Qualcomm carry the cost. ([AMD release](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/AMD/amd-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-7j6jzo29buqw.html), [TradingKey (call)](https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262270388-), [Phil Stock World](https://www.philstockworld.com/2026/11/03/after-hours-earnings-recap-amd-amgn-anet-alab-and-tost/))

**Nov 2 update:** Apple turned Intel's memory warning into a pattern. It said memory pricing is "unprecedented", that most of its December-quarter margin drop comes from memory, and that costs keep rising beyond December; it is offsetting with price increases and cheaper inventory that will run out. That is the clearest pricing-power signal yet for Micron and SK Hynix, and a cost warning for every device and server maker. The market sold chips anyway: the semiconductor ETF fell 3.8%, AMD 7.5%, Micron 5.8% and Intel 8.8%. ([9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/02/apple-says-memory-costs-and-siri-ai-will-weigh-on-holiday-quarter-profit-margins/), [Wall Street Republic](https://thewallstreetrepublic.substack.com/p/marvell-sinks-1272-on-a-115bn-lumentum))

| --- | --- | --- |
| [AMD](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/AMD/amd-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-7j6jzo29buqw.html) | Q3 $13.4B (+45%) vs. \~$13.1B consensus; data center $8.5B (+97%); Q4 guide \~$17B ±3% vs. \~$16.2B; 2027 revenue >80% growth; +7.0–7.6% after hours | Helios racks running at Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle, with HPE, Dell, Lenovo and Super Micro shipping in Q4; PCs are the weak spot |
| Nvidia (NVDA) | Reports Nov 17 after close (confirmed); implied ±8.9% (Nov 2); rose \~2% Tuesday | AMD confirms demand exceeds supply; the debate moves to share of a bigger pie. Amazon and Google also sell their own chips |
| Micron (MU) | 2027 HBM largely sold out at "much higher" prices; up \~3–4% Tuesday | AMD is securing DDR5 and other memory and passing some cost to customers: pricing power confirmed by a second big buyer after Apple |
| SK Hynix (SKHY, Nasdaq ADR) | Says DRAM and HBM sold out through 2029 | Same thesis; TrendForce sees DRAM contract prices up another 10–15% in Q4 |
| TSMC (TSM) | Q3 revenue $46.7B, above guidance | AMD is chasing wafers, substrates and advanced packaging; every chip designer's beat lands here |
| Broadcom (AVGO) | \~$63B AI compute financing reported; up \~3% Tuesday | Arista's beat and guide support its Ethernet switch chips; custom TPU and XPU work competes with AMD and Nvidia |
| Marvell (MRVL) | Buying Lumentum for $115B in stock; fell 12.7% Nov 2 | Dilution and integration risk vs. owning more of the optics chain; a custom-chip supplier to Amazon |
| [Intel (INTC)](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/intel-q3-2026-slides-record-data-center-growth-stock-tumbles-on-outlook-93CH-4985517) | Q4 guide $15B–$16B; supply-limited into H1 2027; \~−28% on Oct 30 | AMD's server share gains come partly at Intel's expense; both now flag PC weakness from memory costs |

**Most likely to move (next 1–2 weeks):** Nvidia, Tuesday after the close (±8.6–9.2%), its first report under interim CEO Colette Kress after Jensen Huang resigned on Nov 12. The stock fell 12.75% last week to $162.85, about 32% below its Oct 6 record, and at least ten analysts moved to Hold. Consensus is about $2.47 EPS on about $109B of revenue; Wedbush expects a beat and a Q4 guide above the Street. AMD and Broadcom are the mirror: up 45% and 25% in five days as the Nvidia alternative, then down 8.8% and 4.8% on Friday. Memory (MU, SNDK) sits between sold-out HBM and buyers' cost pushback. Upside trigger: a beat and raise with Kress reaffirming hyperscaler orders lifts NVDA, TSM and MU, and AMD and AVGO may lag as the rotation reverses. Downside: an in-line guide or tighter China rules (Bessent's chip "leakage" remarks, the Megaspeed entity-list question) send NVDA toward Thursday's \~$149 low and the rotation into AMD and AVGO resumes. Disclosure: AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Nvidia and TSMC are in Anthropic's $26B IPO placement, AMD names Anthropic (which makes me) as an anchor customer and Nvidia is an Anthropic investor; weigh my framing. ([FinanceFeeds](https://financefeeds.com/nvidia-nvda-stock-162-85-saturday-week-ahead-q3-results-17-november-first-under-kress-bull-187-bear-149/), [EarningsWatcher](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/nvda-earnings-november-2026), [CNBC (Huang resigns)](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/nvidia-nvda-jensen-huang-second-affair.html), [RTTNews](https://www.rttnews.com/3712632/anthropic-sets-ipo-price-range-at-70-78-per-share-launches-roadshow.aspx))

**Risk:** Memory was the most crowded trade in the October selloff. SK Hynix fell 9.6% in one session during that slide, so the downside is just as sharp.

**Disclosure:** Some Broadcom financing reporting ties these deals to Anthropic, the company that makes me. I note it so you can weigh my framing.

sections.title: AI software
sections.markdown:
Palantir showed how high the bar is: revenue up 96%, a full-year raise and U.S. commercial passing U.S. government for the first time, and the stock fell 3.1% into the print and barely moved after. ServiceNow's drop last week shows the AI-disruption trade against seat-based software is not over either. In a chip selloff, even AI-outcome software trades with the AI complex.

| Company | Setup | Why it moves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Palantir (PLTR) | Q3: revenue $2.31B (+96%) vs. \~$2.17–2.18B est.; adj. EPS $0.44 vs. \~$0.40–0.41; full-year guide raised to \~$8.53B from as high as $8.2B; U.S. commercial $984M (+148%); contract value $2.92B, only +6% | Beat and raise was priced in; slowing contract value is the new question at a 100x+ multiple |
| ServiceNow (NOW) | Q3 subscription revenue $3.99B (+21%, +20.5% cc) vs. \~20% guide; AI contract-value target raised to $1.7B from $1B; Q4 guide below the Street; fell more than 20% on Oct 29 | Disruption fear won again despite beats on growth and AI |
| Microsoft (MSFT) | Copilot adoption and its own models, alongside Azure | Copilot adoption is the seat-based test of AI monetization; no new data this week |
**Most likely to move (week of Nov 16):** Palo Alto (Wednesday after close, ±11.1–11.3%) and Intuit (Thursday after close, ±9.1–9.4%, rich against its ±6.6% average), with the Anthropic IPO as the sector's supply event (disclosure below). Software held up better than chips on Friday (IGV −0.3% vs SMH −3.0%), but the hike odds still weigh on high multiples, and Microsoft is digesting its Outlook and Teams outage and Anthropic's push into Office-style software. Upside trigger: Palo Alto shows AI-security demand in next-gen ARR and Intuit shows AI agents adding revenue, and the IPO is absorbed without draining peers. Downside: another Palo Alto guide disappointment (it fell 9.3% last time), a hot rates week, or money rotating out of PLTR, NOW and MSFT to fund IPO allocations. ([EarningsWatcher (PANW)](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/panw-earnings-november-2026), [EarningsWatcher (INTU)](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/intu-earnings-november-2026); Friday's moves from Trade Desk's Nov 13 close review)

**Sector event:** Anthropic set its IPO range at $70–78 a share for 801.35 million new Class A shares (plus 23.65 million from selling holders), roughly $56–63B of new money at the range by my arithmetic, to list on Nasdaq as ANT. Reports put pricing on Nov 18 and the first trade on Nov 19, about 6x covered. AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC agreed to buy $26B of stock at the IPO price. Its compute commitments are demand for the chip, memory and cloud names in this report; a listing this large can also pull money from existing AI software stocks. ([RTTNews](https://www.rttnews.com/3712632/anthropic-sets-ipo-price-range-at-70-78-per-share-launches-roadshow.aspx), [Market News, Nov 14](https://hervecuviliez.substack.com/p/market-news-saturday-14-november))

**Disclosure:** I'm built by Anthropic, so I'm not a neutral source on that IPO. I won't give a view on it; treat it purely as a sector catalyst.

sections.title: Oil and gas
sections.markdown:
Exxon and Chevron beat on refining, not crude, and both stocks rose only about 2% premarket, inside implied moves. The next 1–2 weeks still hinge on Iran, and refiners and E&Ps carry the most exposure in both directions. Headline numbers are in the Oct 30 morning brief.

| Company | Latest data point | Why it moves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Valero (VLO), Marathon (MPC), Phillips 66 (PSX) | Fell 7–9% on Oct 27 when fuel prices dropped faster than crude after Trump's "plummeting" post and talk of a Russian-diesel waiver. XOM ran U.S. Gulf Coast refineries at 100% and CVX at \~98% | Most leveraged to crack spreads, both ways; MPC reports Nov 3 |
| Exxon (XOM) | Refining (Energy Products) out-earned upstream; production 4,496 koebd, slightly down q/q; $20B buyback planned for 2027 | Buybacks and debt cuts cushion a price drop; +2.1% premarket vs. ±3.9% implied |
| Chevron (CVX) | Adj. EPS $5.28 vs. $4.78 est.; downstream $3.58B vs. $638M a year ago; capex fell as Permian spending eased | Same cushion as XOM; trades on the Q4 margin outlook |
| E&Ps (COP, OXY, EOG) | Brent \~$117 and WTI \~$104 Friday morning after Hormuz mine claims | Purest crude exposure with no refining offset; biggest movers on Iran headlines |
| SLB, HAL, BKR | Majors are cutting Permian spending and returning cash instead | Services lag the oil price; HAL is most tied to U.S. land drilling |

**Most likely to move (week of Nov 16):** Refiners (VLO, MPC) and E&Ps (OXY, COP) on Sunday night's reopen. Over the weekend the IRGC said it sent six drones at a US air defense radar at Riffa Air Base in Bahrain (Bahrain says it intercepted several), after a Friday claim the US denied. Iran also says tankers hit mines in Hormuz, including one supertanker it says sank; the US says it has cleared the main routes. Talks are stalled: Iran awaits a US reply to its seven conditions sent through Qatar. Against that, Brent settled at $95.84 Friday after a second weekly loss, the IEA says the market is back in surplus, and Hormuz traffic is still about 65% below pre-war levels. Upside trigger: trackers or insurers confirm the strikes or the US retaliates, and Brent clears \~$98. Downside: the claims fade as Friday's did and Brent slides toward \~$91, refiners first. ([Al Jazeera](https://aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/15/iran-says-it-targets-us-radar-in-bahrain-what-do-we-know), [FinanceFeeds](https://financefeeds.com/brent-crude-oil-price-95-84-sunday-futures-open-week-ahead-iran-mine-claims-bull-98-bear-91/), [RTÉ (supertanker claim)](https://rte.ie/news/middle-east/2026/1115/1599293-iran-tanker-hormuz))

**Nov 3 update:** oil whipsawed. Brent rose early (to \~$106.50) on reports of a U.S. strike on an Iranian Revolutionary Guard position on Qeshm Island after a missile was fired at a U.S. aircraft, then slipped back to \~$103–104 (WTI \~$95–96) on talk of progress toward a U.S.–Iran deal, even as Reuters cited an Iranian official saying the sides remain far apart. Marathon Petroleum's Q3 showed what refiners are earning while it lasts: adjusted EPS $26.93, a $45.70/bbl refining margin at 100% utilization, and another $5B of buybacks. The midterms add no direct oil signal yet; the Iran headlines still set direction, and refiners remain the most leveraged both ways. ([TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-nov-03-2026), [StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/stock-market-today-live-november-3-2026), [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-tuesday-november-3-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-midterms-amd-earnings-141143244.html), [Marathon Petroleum 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001510295/000151029526000069/mpcq32026earningsrelease.htm))

**Both directions:** Upside if the weekend strikes are confirmed, the US answers them, or Iran keeps Hormuz shut while waiting on its seven conditions: Brent back above \~$98 and refiners and E&Ps extend. Downside if the claims fade and the surplus wins, or Washington and Tehran move toward a version of Qatar's plan: refiners fall first and hardest, as on Oct 27 and Nov 4, then E\&Ps; XOM and CVX lose least.
